page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-core ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The architecture assigns 1 dedicated physical core per vCPU with no simultaneous multithreading, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity sits at 128.0 GB, yielding a compute-tailored 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES instructions, maintains a baseline network throughput of 133 Gbps, and omits integrated local storage and GPU accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate competitive multi-core parallelism and memory throughput across intensive workloads. While single-core evaluations such as stress-ng (1706.49) and Geekbench (1890.0) fall in the middle tier, the instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core Geekbench (25948.0) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (669.84 GB/sec). Memory throughput is especially pronounced, reaching 466.21 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB reads and 210.01 GB/sec in writes. Database and web serving tests perform strongly, with PassMark database operations at 47513.78, Redis SET processing reaching 133.04 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput hitting 113.57 GB/sec.

Architectural tradeoffs center on reliance on external network-attached storage and the absence of discrete matrix and vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 or AMX. Large language model inference speeds reflect this: prompt processing and smaller model text generation test in the middle to lower tiers, though medium (7B) and large (70B) model text generation register in the upper quartile. With a high core count and high network throughput, the c8gb.16xlarge represents an efficient multi-threaded compute profile suited for continuous integration build farms, Clang software compilation, Redis in-memory caching, web serving fleets, and scalable parallel data processing.
